'''Berend (Bert) Poolman''' is a Dutch [[biochemist]],  as specialist in [[bioenergetics]] of microorganisms and [[membrane transport]]. He is a [[professor]] of Biochemistry at the [[University of Groningen]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Prof. Dr. B. (Bert) Poolman|url=https://www.rug.nl/staff/b.poolman/|publisher=RUG|access-date=19 February 2020}}</ref> and an elected member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (KNAW) since 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/7959 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200217155156/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/7959 |title=Bert Poolman |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |archive-date=17 February 2020}}</ref> Poolman is a pioneer in the  field of bottom-up [[synthetic biology]], that is, the construction from molecular building blocks of functional [[metabolic networks]] and autonomously operating functional systems, which are typical of living cells. Poolman is a [[lecturer]] in membrane biology and synthetic biology.

== Education and career ==
Poolman pursued studies in Biochemistry and [[Microbiology]] at the University of Groningen, the Netherlands, and the [[University of Bern]] ([[Switzerland]]), obtaining a [[MSc degree]] in 1984. He gained his [[PhD]] in 1987 with a thesis on  bioenergetics of [[streptococci]], under the supervision of  Wil Konings and  Hans Veldkamp.<ref>{{cite web|title=Energy transducing processes in growing and starving lactic acid streptococcci |url=https://www.rug.nl/research/portal/files/3392440/poolman.PDF|author=B. Poolman|publisher=RUG|access-date=19 February 2020}}</ref>
After a brief stint as a scientist at [[Genencor International|Genencor Inc]] (now Dupont Industrial Biosciences) in [[San Francisco]] (USA), he returned to the Netherlands in the end of 1989 to start his own research group on biochemistry and molecular biology of membrane transport at the University of Groningen, supported by a [[fellowship]] from the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences. He has been professor of biochemistry at the  Groningen since 1998.<ref>{{cite web|title=Prof. Dr. B. (Bert) Poolman, Hoogleraar Biochemie |url=https://www.rug.nl/staff/b.poolman/|publisher=RUG|access-date=19 February 2020}}</ref> In 2008 he was appointed Program Director of its Centre for Synthetic Biolog),<ref>{{cite journal|title=477 Ru Groningen Start Onderzoekscentrum Synthetische Biologie|publisher=Springer|doi=10.1007/BF03096713|year=2008|journal=Zorg en Financiering|volume=7|issue=4|pages=110–111|s2cid=195377380 }}</ref> and in 2013 he became Scientific Director of its Biomolecular Sciences and Biotechnology Institute.<ref>{{cite web|title=Management|date=15 February 2016 |url=https://www.rug.nl/research/gbb/organisation/management-team|publisher=RUG|access-date=19 February 2020}}</ref>
In 1993 Poolman has done a [[sabbatical]] at Transgene SA, Strasbourg (France). Thanks to a [[Fulbright fellowship]], he was visiting professor in biochemistry at [[California Institute of Technology]], [[Pasadena]] (USA) in 2003.

Poolman has been Chair of the [[KNAW]] Earth and Life Sciences Board, and has been vice-chair of KNAW Council for Natural and Technical Sciences since 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Member of KNAW Council for Natural and Technical Sciences|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/advisory-work/advisory-councils-and-committees/15276/akademiaorganisation_membersview|publisher=KNAW|access-date=17 February 2020|archive-date=17 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200217155121/https://www.knaw.nl/en/advisory-work/advisory-councils-and-committees/15276/akademiaorganisation_membersview|url-status=dead}}</ref>
From 2016 to 2018, he was a member of the Dutch Council for Physics and Chemistry,<ref>{{cite web|title=Wie zijn wij?|url=http://raadns.nl/wie-zijn-wij|publisher=Raad voor de Natuur- en Scheikunde|access-date=19 February 2020|archive-date=26 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190926110911/http://raadns.nl/wie-zijn-wij|url-status=dead}}</ref> and currently he is a member of the core team of the Council for Chemistry.<ref>{{cite web|title=Members KNAW |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members#b_start=0&c3=P |publisher=KNAW|access-date=17 February 2020}}</ref>
Since 2009 he led the focus area on ‘Biomolecular and Bioinspired Functionality’ at the [[Zernike Institute for Advanced Materials]] (University of Groningen, together with [[Nobel laureate]] [[Ben Feringa]], and, from 2010 to 2017, he managed a national Synthetic Biology program of the University of Groningen.<ref>{{cite web |title=ZI-NRC focus areas |date=14 June 2019 |url=https://www.rug.nl/research/zernike/research/zi-nrc-research-program|publisher=RUG |access-date=6 March 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Prof. Dr. Bert Poolman|url=https://www.membraneenzymology.com/poolman/|publisher=Membrane Enzymology|access-date=6 March 2020}}.</ref>

== Research ==
Poolman has made seminal contributions to the understanding of the dynamics and [[Semipermeable membrane|permeability]] of biological membranes<ref>{{cite web|title=Mechanisms of membrane toxicity of hydrocarbons|url=https://www.rug.nl/research/portal/files/10534859/1995MicrobiolRevSikkema.pdf|publisher=RUG|access-date=1 March 2020|archive-date=1 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200301125204/https://www.rug.nl/research/portal/files/10534859/1995MicrobiolRevSikkema.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Lateral Diffusion of Membrane Proteins|publisher=ACS Publications|doi=10.1021/ja902853g|pmid=19673517|year=2009|last1=Ramadurai|first1=Sivaramakrishnan|last2=Holt|first2=Andrea|last3=Krasnikov|first3=Victor|last4=Van Den Bogaart|first4=Geert|last5=Killian|first5=J. Antoinette|last6=Poolman|first6=Bert|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=131|issue=35|pages=12650–12656 |bibcode=2009JAChS.13112650R }}</ref> and to the field of [[Vector (molecular biology)|vectorial biochemistry]], that is,  the role of electrochemical gradients in the fuelling and regulation of [[membrane transport]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Regulation of Solute Transport in Streptococci by External and Internal pH Values |url=https://www.rug.nl/research/portal/files/3385954/1987MicrobiolRevPoolman.pdf|publisher=RUG|access-date=1 March 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Regulation of bacterial sugar-H+ symport by phosphoenolpyruvate-dependent enzyme I/HPrmediated phosphorylation|url=https://www.rug.nl/research/portal/files/13641274/1995ProcNatlAcadSciPoolman.pdf|publisher=RUG|access-date=1 March 2020}}</ref> He demonstrated that the exchange of different sugars can be more advantageous for a cell than sugar-proton symport, and showed that cells exploit the coupling of substrate import to product exchange to conserve [[metabolic]] energy.<ref>{{cite web|title=Arginine transport in Streptococcus lactis is catalyzed by a cationic exchanger|url=https://www.rug.nl/research/portal/files/3384968/1987ProcNatlAcadSciDriessen.pdf|publisher=RUG|access-date=1 March 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Malolactic Fermentation |url=https://www.rug.nl/research/portal/files/3348307/1991JBacteriolPoolman.pdf |publisher=RUG|access-date=1 March 2020}}</ref>

He is an expert in the field of [[ATP-binding cassette transporter]]s, one of the largest known protein families, by combining functional and structural studies. Highlights include: discovery of export of [[hydrophobic]] [[Chemical compound|compounds]] from the inner leaflet of the [[lipid bilayer]];<ref>{{cite journal|title=Multidrug resistance in Lactococcus lactis: evidence for ATP-dependent drug extrusion from the inner leaflet of the cytoplasmic membrane.|publisher=EMBO Press|doi=10.1002/j.1460-2075.1996.tb00798.x|year=1996|last1=Bolhuis|first1=H.|last2=Van Veen|first2=H. == Current research (2020) ==
His main current research areas include: (i) bacterial cell-volume regulation: elucidation of the [[homeostatic]] mechanisms that control the [[physicochemistry]] of the cell;<ref>{{cite journal|title=Microorganisms maintain crowding homeostasis |publisher=Nature Reviews|doi=10.1038/nrmicro.2017.17|pmid=28344349|year=2017|last1=Van Den Berg|first1=Jonas|last2=Boersma|first2=Arnold J.|last3=Poolman|first3=Bert|journal=Nature Reviews Microbiology|volume=15|issue=5|pages=309–318|s2cid=7829229 |url=https://research.rug.nl/en/publications/4f9459bf-3318-496e-918f-3154457ad108 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Ribosome surface properties may impose limits on the nature of the cytoplasmic proteome|publisher=E LIFE|doi=10.7554/eLife.30084.001|doi-access=free}}</ref> (ii) building of [[Synthetic biology|synthetic]] cells: construction of functional out-of-[[Equilibrium chemistry|equilibrium]] systems for metabolic energy conservation and development of cell volume regulatory networks.<ref>{{cite journal|title=A synthetic metabolic network for physicochemical homeostasis|journal=Nature Communications|doi=10.1038/s41467-019-12287-2|doi-access=free|pmid=31534136|pmc=6751199|year=2019|last1=Pols|first1=Tjeerd|last2=Sikkema|first2=Hendrik R.|last3=Gaastra|first3=Bauke F.|last4=Frallicciardi|first4=Jacopo|last5=Śmigiel|first5=Wojciech M.|last6=Singh|first6=Shubham|last7=Poolman|first7=Bert|volume=10|issue=1|pages=4239|bibcode=2019NatCo..10.4239P }}</ref> What tasks should a living cell minimally perform and how this can be accomplished with a minimal set of components? and (iii) the molecular mechanisms of membrane transport [[proteins]]: understanding the dynamics, energetics and mechanisms of [[solute transporters]] in the [[plasma membrane]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Steric exclusion and protein conformation determine the localization of plasma membrane transporters|publisher=Springer Nature Communications|doi=10.1038/s41467-018-02864-2|pmid=29402931|year=2018|last1=Bianchi|first1=Frans|last2=Syga|first2=Łukasz|last3=Moiset|first3=Gemma|last4=Spakman|first4=Dian|last5=Schavemaker|first5=Paul E.|last6=Punter|first6=Christiaan M.|last7=Seinen|first7=Anne-Bart|last8=Van Oijen|first8=Antoine M.|last9=Robinson|first9=Andrew|last10=Poolman|first10=Bert|journal=Nature Communications|volume=9|issue=1 |page=501 |pmc=5799302 |bibcode=2018NatCo...9..501B |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Conformational and dynamic plasticity in substrate-binding proteins underlies selective transport in ABC importers|publisher=eLIFE|doi=10.7554/eLife.44652.001|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Publications ==
*  Poolman is [[Institute for Scientific Information|ISI]] highly [[cited]] researcher in microbiology. He has published over 275 [[peer-reviewed]] papers in international scientific journals,<ref>{{cite web|title=Publicaties B. Poolman |url=https://www.rug.nl/staff/b.poolman/research/publications.html|publisher=Rijksuniversiteit Groningen |access-date=17 February 2020}}</ref> which have been cited more than 25,000 times. His [[H-index]] ([[Google Scholar]]) is 83,<ref>{{cite web|title=Poolman B|url=https://scholar.google.nl/citations?user=GQObZz0AAAAJ&hl=nl|publisher=Google Scholar|access-date=17 February 2020}}</ref> and he holds four [[patents]]. Poolman shares his findings with wide audiences through newspaper, radio and TV appearances. In 2012 Schrauwers and Poolman wrote the book ''Synthetische Biologie: de Mens als Schepper'' (''Synthetic Biology: Man as a Creator'') to convey the developments in synthetic biology to a lay audience.<ref>{{cite web|title=Synthetische Biologie: de Mens als Schepper|url=https://www.bol.com/nl/p/wetenschappelijke-bibliotheek-112-synthetische-biologie/1001004011500414/|publisher=Bol.com|access-date=17 February 2020}}</ref>

== Awards and fellowships ==
Poolman has received numerous awards, including the Biochemistry Award (1989) of the ''Dutch Biochemistry and Molecular Biology Organisation'' (NVBMB),<ref>{{cite web|title=NVBMB Prize|url=https://nvbmb.kncv.nl/prizes/nvbmb-prize|publisher=NVBMB|access-date=17 February 2020}}</ref> a [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] [[fellowship]] (1989), a ''Human Frontiers Science Program Organization'' award (1992),<ref>{{cite web|title=Our mission|url=https://www.hfsp.org/|publisher=HFSP|access-date=19 February 2020}}</ref> the SON ‘Jonge Chemici’ award (1997), the Federation European Biochemical Society Lecturer Award (2014),<ref>{{cite web |title=FEBS: advancing molecular life sciences |url=https://www.febs.org/ |publisher=FEBS |access-date=19 February 2020}}</ref> and the [[Joel Mandelstam]] Memorial Lecture award (2016).<ref>{{cite web|title=Oxford Talks |url=https://talks.ox.ac.uk/talks/department/id/oxpoints:23232534?show_all=true|publisher=University of Oxford|access-date=19 February 2020}}</ref>

He obtained four TOP program grants from the [[Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research]] (NWO)(2001, 2007, 2010, 2014).,<ref>{{cite web|title=NWO Chemistry of Life Factsheet 2015-2016|url=https://www.nwo.nl/binaries/content/documents/nwo/algemeen/documentation/application/cw/hoofdlijnen-cw/nwo-chemistry-of-life-factsheet/NWO+Chemistry+of+Life+FS-pdf.pdf|publisher=NWO|access-date=19 February 2020}}{{Dead link|date=May 2021 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=TOP-PUNT Grant for Poolman|date=17 September 2014 |url=https://www.rug.nl/news/2014/09/top-punt-grant-for-poolman|publisher=RUG|access-date=19 February 2020}}</ref> two program grants from the [[Netherlands Proteomics Centre]] (2005 en 2008),<ref>{{cite web |title=Analytical Hotel Groningen |url=http://www.netherlandsproteomicscentre.nl/npc/research-hotels/analytical-hotel-groningen.html?searched=Poolman&advsearch=oneword&highlight=ajaxSearch_highlight+ajaxSearch_highlight1 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130629182304/https://netherlandsproteomicscentre.nl/npc/research-hotels/analytical-hotel-groningen.html |archive-date=29 Jun 2013 |access-date=19 February 2020 |publisher=netherlands proteomics centre}}</ref> and coordinated three large European networks (1996, 1999 and 2012). In 2015 he received an [[ERC Advanced Grant]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Twee Europese subsidies voor fundamenteel biochemisch onderzoek |date=22 April 2015 |url=https://www.rug.nl/news/2015/04/twee-europese-subsidies-voor-fundamenteel-biochemisch-onderzoek|publisher=RUG|access-date=19 February 2020}}</ref> and in 2019 an [[European Research Council|ERC]] Proof-of-Concept Grant,<ref>{{cite web|title=List of selected principal investigators|url=https://erc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/document/file/erc-2019-PoC-third-round-list-of-selected-researchers.pdf|publisher=ERC|access-date=19 February 2020}}</ref> and in 2017 the BaSyC consortium (with Poolman as one of the lead principal investigators) was awarded a multimillion Dutch Gravitation grant.<ref>{{cite web|title=BaSyC - Building a Synthetic Cell |url=https://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/research-projects/i/45/29045.html|publisher=NWO|access-date=1 March 2020}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Poolman was born in 1959 as the first son of Jelto Poolman and Neeltje Prinsse. In 1983 he married Heleen Stevenson (1959), with whom he has four children.
